change_summary: The journal published an expression of concern about the paper "Gut bacteria and mood in mice", and the editors have received concerns about some of the data reported in the article. The matter is still being looked into, and the editors will update readers when they know more, so the paper's data are in doubt, but they have not been withdrawn and no conclusion has been reached yet. The notice does not say which data, figures or results the concerns are about, so it is unclear whether they affect the main forced-swim result in Figure 3 or other data such as the bacterial counts in Figure 4. The paper's main result is that mice given gut bacteria from depressed donors were less active in a forced-swim test, shown in Figure 3, while the paper also reports bacterial counts in Figure 4.
evaluation: Your Discussion cites Lopez and Chen [8] as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, in support of a causal role of gut bacteria in depressive behaviour, and you say your own proposal builds on this finding. The paper reports this as recipient mice being less active in a forced-swim test after transplant of gut bacteria from depressed donors, shown in Figure 3. The journal's editors issued an expression of concern saying they have received concerns about some of the data reported in the article, but the notice does not say which data, figures or results the concerns are about, so it is unclear whether they touch the reduced-activity finding your Discussion relies on. The matter is still being looked into, and the editors will update readers when they know more, so the impact on your draft is medium, and uncertain: your proposal builds on a finding that may or may not be among the questioned data, and no conclusion has been reached yet.
recommendation: Your draft's Discussion cites Lopez and Chen [8] as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, in support of a causal role of gut bacteria in depressive behaviour, and your draft says its own proposal builds on this finding. The journal's editors issued an expression of concern saying they have received concerns about some of the data reported in the article, but the notice does not say which data, figures or results the concerns are about, so it is unclear whether the concerns touch the reduced-activity finding your Discussion relies on. Hedge that Discussion sentence and cite the expression of concern. Don't build new work on the finding until the editors report back, and check with co-authors or your supervisor how much your proposal depends on it. I'll keep tracking the paper, so a later retraction or correction would raise a new alert.
